subject: Partial streaming responses & elevated p99 — customer notice and remediation plan
messages:
From: Alicia Ramos <alicia@luminahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: support@luminahealth.com
Date: 2028-11-11T08:12:00-05:00
Subject: Partial streamed responses from hosted API (sample request IDs attached)

Jonas —

We started seeing an increase in partial streamed responses and stalls on our production integration starting ~07:50 EST. Symptoms: the model emits the first chunk of tokens and then the stream freezes for 10–30s, sometimes followed by a 502 or a duplicated final token. This is affecting our real-time summarization flow.

Attached is an ops snapshot (ops_snapshot_20281111.txt) with 3 request IDs and the request payloads. Example request id: rq_20281111_LH_3pz1 (we attached the server-side trace IDs).

Can you confirm if there's a known degradation on the hosted inference side? If this requires us to switch to a different region or model variant while you investigate, please advise an ETA.

We rely on sub-second tail behavior for a portion of our traffic — impact here is visible in our metrics and choking our downstream consumers.

Thanks —
Alicia Ramos
Head of Platform, Lumina Health
Alicia.Ramos@luminahealth.com

[attachment: ops_snapshot_20281111.txt]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-11T08:28:00-05:00
Subject: Fwd: Partial streamed responses from hosted API (Lumina) — triage and status post draft

Team — forwarding Lumina's report. I pulled the traces Alicia sent and see repeated partial-chunk handoffs with matching edge request ids. Initial guess: a multipath routing imbalance between our prefetch layer and the streaming fanout that occasionally leaves the client connection pinned to a cold backend.

Action items (short):
- Sean: enable targeted routing fallback for Lumina's account to a single-path low-volume model variant in us-east-1 for 15m to see if the freeze disappears. Use policy: account_id = lumina -> route to variant v1-prefetch-off.
- Monica: prepare a terse status page entry and a customer-facing note describing observed impact and immediate mitigation. Keep it factual; no root cause yet.
- Marissa: start timeline capture and collect more traces (I flagged three sample request ids in the snapshot).

Draft status page blurb (quick):
"We are investigating reports of partial/paused streaming responses affecting a subset of hosted API requests in us-east-1. A remediation path has been applied for impacted customers and we will provide updates as we validate stability."

I'll coordinate the go/no-go to publish; want to avoid alarming customers with speculation. Targeting an ETA to Lumina within 20 minutes.

-Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-11T08:45:00-05:00
Subject: RE: Partial streamed responses from hosted API (Lumina) — immediate mitigation and status page entry

Alicia —

Thanks for the quick heads up and for the trace bundle. We see the same pattern in our telemetry and have applied an immediate, targeted mitigation for your account. Summary of what we did: 

- Applied per-account routing fallback that pins Lumina traffic to a single-path model variant (v1-stable) in us-east-1 to avoid the multipath fanout path for 15 minutes.
- Lifted aggressive prefetch/parallelization for your account to reduce concurrent KV cache handoffs.
- Created a temporary rate-limit buffer on parallel streaming connections to smooth downstream consumption.

Observed effect: preliminary sampling shows a 90% reduction in stream stalls for affected requests within the first 5 minutes. We will monitor for 30 minutes and re-evaluate.

We have posted a short notice on our status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/20281111-multipath-io
(You'll find the entry under "Partial streaming behavior — us-east-1"; the notice is intentionally concise while we collect more telemetry.)

If you prefer, we can also failover your integration to our dedicated variant in us-west (will require a brief config change on your side) — let me know and we can schedule.

Next update: 09:15 EST with additional telemetry and whether we will extend the routing change.

-Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia@luminahealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-12T10:05:00-05:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: Partial streaming stalls — us-east-1 (Lumina Health)

Alicia —

Thanks for your patience while we investigated. Below is a concise post-incident summary and our follow-up items. If you'd like a more formal postmortem with diagrams, we can share the full report and a walkthrough call.

What happened (summary):
- Between ~07:48–09:10 EST on 2028-11-11, a subset of hosted streaming requests in us-east-1 experienced intermittent partial-token emissions followed by stalls. The issue manifested most frequently for sessions using aggressive client-side parallel reads + the prefetch fanout policy.
- Root cause (high level): an edge-caching race between prefetch fanout and our streaming aggregator caused occasional partial KV cache handoffs. This left some streams pinned to a backend that had not completed prefix materialization, resulting in pauses and, in some cases, duplicate tail tokens.

Actions taken during the incident:
- Applied per-account routing fallback to a single-path variant for affected customers (Lumina) — immediate improvement observed.
- Disabled aggressive prefetch for the impacted traffic paths and introduced a short buffer on parallel streaming connections.
- Created a concise status page entry and kept impacted customers informed.

Customer impact:
- Partial or paused streams for ~2% of total requests during the window. Latency p95 increased for streaming sessions by ~1.8s on average for affected requests. No data loss reported.

Follow-ups / remediation plan:
1) Engineering (Sean & infra): implement a hardened prefetch handoff that enforces prefix materialization acknowledgment before streaming routing completes (ETA: 3 sprints).
2) Product (Jonas & Marissa): expand our per-account routing playbooks to allow automated 30-min fallbacks for high-impact customers and surface a suggestion in the Console for customers with strict tail latency needs (ETA: 6 weeks).
3) Observability (Monica): add a focused dashboard and alert for multipath handoffs that shows per-account stall rates and correlated KV cache misses (ETA: 2 weeks).

Attachments: timeline and sample traces (timeline-lumina-incident-20281111.pdf).

We sincerely apologize for the disruption and appreciate Lumina's detailed traces — they materially sped up the investigation. If you're open to a 30-minute walkthrough, we can schedule a session this week to run through the timeline and planned mitigations.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Reliability
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
